access.admission: A device or private runner reaches the same central cache listener through an estate-admitted remote-access forward, such as restricted SSH or rds forward. Redundant routes share that central store; no route falls back to a public source. Host, ticket, port and admitted identities live in the private estate.

integrity: The cache commits an object only after a complete download; OCI digest paths and checksum-pinned GitHub assets additionally require the named SHA-256. It generates crates.io index config.json and rewrites download links in PyPI and pub documents to the client's loopback base. npm links stay public, except that Bun gets the public registry's tarball links empty and builds them from its configured registry; artifact bytes stay unchanged. Clients keep their own digest and signature checks.

routes.objects: Distribution components and rustup releases; channel manifests are revalidated.
Flutter SDK, engine and Dart SDK archives and the Flutter Maven repository; release indexes and Maven metadata are revalidated.

clients.limits: Gradle refuses plain-HTTP Maven repositories without an explicit opt-in, so Android engine artifacts need TLS in front of the forwarded port. Pub packages are a later increment.

routes.objects: CPython release archives of dated release tags.

Public uploaded release assets under exact owner/repository/releases/download/tag/asset paths, with a caller-pinned SHA-256 in the cache URL. Only bytes matching that digest are committed. An escaped slash is allowed only within the release tag.

clients.limits: Public assets only; no API, latest-release resolution, caller authentication, source archives or automatic URL rewriting. The consumer keeps its own size, digest and signature checks and must not retry a public URL after a cache failure.

routes.objects: Playwright browser and tool builds.

clients.limits: Keep distributionSha256Sum. Whether the wrapper accepts a plain-HTTP distributionUrl is not verified.

clients.limits: GOTOOLCHAIN downloads go through the goproxy route instead.

clients.limits: Version indexes on googlechromelabs.github.io are not proxied; resolve the version upstream or from a pinned lock.

routes.objects: Sparse index files of crates.io; they are revalidated. The cache answers config.json itself and points crate downloads at the crates route of the base address the client used.

clients.limits: Set through cargo --config or a Cargo configuration file: Cargo reads source replacement from no environment variable. Index changes reach clients after the revalidation age. Cargo names its local registry cache by the URL, port included, so a client keeps one forwarded port to reuse it.

routes.objects: Crate archives of exact published versions; Cargo checks each one against the checksum in its index entry.

clients.tool: cargo, through the index configuration the cache generates
clients.limits: No client setting: the config.json of the crates-index route carries this download template.

routes.objects: Package documents in the representation the client accepts, the install document or the full document, revalidated and served with the public tarball links upstream sent, or to Bun as the install document with the public registry's tarball links empty; tarballs of exact published versions, which clients check against the integrity in the document.

clients.limits: nds-cache bind writes the registry into a global configuration file of its own, which npm_config_globalconfig in the environment file names, because Bun reads npm's user file and variables but not that file; npm is bound where the environment file applies. The user's and the project's .npmrc rank above it, and while bound npm reads it in place of its default global file. npm's default replace-registry-host fetches the public tarball links of a package document through the cache, so package-lock.json keeps registry.npmjs.org; a project that sets replace-registry-host to never downloads tarballs directly. Audit, search, login and publish endpoints are not proxied; run npm without audit.

A project or job selects the route with --registry or a default registry in its own .npmrc; the device client leaves Bun unbound, because Bun does not read the npm global configuration file. A User-Agent that opens with Bun/ gets the install document with the tarball links under https://registry.npmjs.org/ empty, which Bun builds from its configured registry, so online and frozen installs download through the cache, and a bun.lock that Bun creates or installs from unchanged records those packages with an empty registry, as a public install does. Bun loads an empty registry as its configured one, so bun add, bun update or an edited package.json through the route write the cache address into the entries the lockfile already held; author those changes against the canonical registry. Scoped registries and their credentials in the project's or job's .npmrc keep precedence and do not pass through the cache. A tarball link to another host stays as upstream sent it.

routes.objects: Project pages of the simple repository API in its JSON form, under normalized project names, revalidated and served with their file links pointed at the pypi-files route of the client's base address.

clients.tool: uv pip install and uv tool install
clients.limits: uv lock through the cache records the forwarded base in uv.lock, and uv treats a lockfile resolved against another index as outdated, so locked project syncs keep the public index.
Only the JSON form is served; a client that accepts only HTML pages gets 406.

routes.objects: Release files and their core metadata files at their digest paths; clients check each file against the hash on its project page.

clients.tool: uv and pip, through the project pages of the pypi route
clients.limits: No client setting: the project pages served by the cache carry these links.

routes.objects: Package documents of the hosted repository API, revalidated and served with their archive links pointed at this route of the client's base address; archives of exact published versions, which pub checks against the archive_sha256 in the document.

clients.limits: pubspec.lock records the forwarded base as the hosted URL, and dart pub get --enforce-lockfile refuses a lockfile resolved against pub.dev, so locked builds keep the public repository. Security advisories are served with the package documents.
The same pub client and lockfile limits as dart pub get; Flutter SDK artifacts use the flutter route.

routes.objects: Release files of the Maven Central layout and their checksums; maven-metadata.xml is revalidated and snapshots are not served.

clients.limits: Accepted as HTTP on the loopback end of an authenticated, encrypted rds forward, not JVM HTTPS. contracts/gradle/nds-cache.init.gradle.kts, passed to one build with --init-script and NDS_CACHE_BASE set to the literal http://127.0.0.1:PORT forward, retargets only the public repositories and sets isAllowInsecureProtocol on those cache URLs alone, with no global disable, trust store or local CA; private or authenticated repositories keep their URLs. It adds no repository beside them, so an unreachable cache fails the build. Use strict dependency verification against checksums that do not come from the cache. Gradle probes repositories in order, so upstream 404s from the earlier ones are expected.

routes.objects: The Go checksum database: lookups and tiles, fixed once published, and the newest signed tree head, revalidated. The cache answers /supported itself, so the go command of a goproxy client reaches the database only here.
Module versions of the Go module proxy protocol: .info, .mod and .zip of exact versions, including golang.org/toolchain for GOTOOLCHAIN; version lists and @latest are revalidated.

clients.tool: go mod download, go build and GOTOOLCHAIN switches
clients.limits: The go command finds the checksum database through this proxy (the gosumdb route) and verifies its signed notes with the database's own key, so keep GOSUMDB enabled. Private modules stay outside through GOPRIVATE.

routes.objects: Image manifests of the docker.io registry, revalidated by tag and content-addressed by digest, and blobs, stored only with the digest their path names.

clients.tool: docker pull and FROM in builds
clients.limits: Clients name the cache's loopback address before the registry, as in 127.0.0.1:PORT/docker.io/NAME:TAG; Docker allows plain HTTP to loopback registries. Docker registry-mirrors cover only Docker Hub and need a daemon restart, and containerd mirrors need hosts.toml, so neither is configured here. Pulls are anonymous; private images keep their own registry.
